scope: private candidate source, isolated Store fixtures, authoritative source metadata, and read-only route/index inspection

findings.title: retirement recovery does not bind victims to the requested registration
findings.evidence: The retirement journal is validated through the same multi-victim branch as eviction. It checks only that after.entries is a subset of before.entries and that registrations omit every registration requiring journal.victims; it does not require exactly one victim, the requested registration, or the requested child entry. A private isolated fixture modified pending.json after retirement:journal to add the unrelated second child to victims and remove its entry/registration. recover() accepted the journal and deleted both target and unrelated entries.
findings.impact: A corrupted or same-owner modified pending retirement can remove unrelated Store entries and registrations, violating the no-unrelated-deletions and recovery/index-integrity requirements.

findings.title: KEEP is not rechecked at the deletion boundary
findings.evidence: Store.retire checks KEEP before journaling, but _delete_owned performs no KEEP check. A private isolated fixture added KEEP from the checkpoint at index, after the journal transition and before payload deletion; retire() still deleted the entry.
findings.impact: A KEEP marker created during the recovery/deletion window cannot stop the in-progress Store-owned deletion, despite KEEP being a required protection.
